#NOWNESSMeets: Frederik Heyman 🐕 Acclaimed visual artist and director shares the inspiration and work processes behind his experimental short film ‘The Scent Remains’ ⁠
⁠
Merging digitally constructed universes, with the physical performance practice of Milou Van Duijnhoven, the film unfolds as a mourning ritual, navigating fragments of memory trapped in repetition and transformation⁠
⁠
Swipe to hear Heyman’s reflections on how the endurance of the human body and mind inspire his work, and the creative possibilities the digital world makes possible for film ⁠
⁠
Tap the link in bio to watch ‘The Scent Remains’ on NOWNESS 🎥⁠
⁠

#Experiments: Merging digitally constructed universes with physical performance, artist Frederik Heyman and performer Milou Van Duijnhoven build a hybrid mourning ritual set inside a black, timeless void, navigating fragments of memory trapped in repetition and transformation⁠
⁠
Carrying the weight of breath and exhaustion, tension and fragility, Van Duijnhoven’s performance places the physical body in a suspended state as the unstable environment shifts around her⁠
⁠
Informed by gaming logic, Heyman uses a first-person camera perspective to establish the presence of an invisible observer who can witness but never intervene, becoming part of the mourning process, and a reflection of Heyman himself⁠
⁠
Tap the link in bio to watch the full film on NOWNESS 🎬⁠
⁠

Performance by @milou.van.duijnhoven⁠

When Andrew Bolton first reached out to @sjodwyer and @karolinevitto about the @metmuseum’s new Costume Institute exhibition, both designers expected to be meeting with an assistant. But each ended up on long, searching calls with Bolton himself – a detail that underpins the seriousness with which Costume Art, the inaugural show in the Costume Institute’s newly expanded galleries, was conceived. ⁠
⁠
Pairing garments with works from across The Met’s collection – etchings, sculpture, painting – the exhibition presents the dressed body as a subject worthy of the same scrutiny as any other art historical question. For O’Dwyer and Vitto, two of the most significant independent designers working with extended sizing in fashion today, being included felt both overdue and, given the current climate, strangely timely. ⁠
⁠
In an exclusive conversation with @mad.e.leiner, the two designers discuss what it means to have this work archived, the words we still haven’t got right, and the “slow-motion car crash” of thinning they’ve both been watching for years. Read more at the link in bio 📲⁠

5,783 contact sheets spanning Peter Hujar’s photographic life are stored in eight banker boxes. Each sheet is encased in a plastic wallet, separated, and sorted vertically like documents in a filing cabinet. ⁠
⁠
There is nothing especially remarkable about these prosaic boxes: colourless, functional, quietly banal. They could easily be passed over without a second glance. Yet inside, they hold an entire world. On the occasion of Hujar: Contact, a new book published by @mack_publishing alongside an exhibition of the same name at @themorganlibrary and Museum, curator Joel Smith and archivist @olivia.mc speak to both the artistic and personal intimacy of Hujar’s contact sheets.⁠
⁠
“Nothing that supersedes the intimacy of the contact sheets themselves,” McCall tells @w.lliam. Read the interview at the link in bio 📲⁠
⁠
📸 Hujar: Contact. Courtesy of MACK; Fraenkel Gallery, San Francisco; and Ortuzar, New York. © The Peter Hujar Archive / Artists Rights Society (ARS)⁠

@cary.kwok is known for playful erotic paintings and sculptures featuring towering phallic forms and profusions of glistening ejaculate. His works often combine human-made objects with the body, touching on everything from furniture design to fashion illustration and speculative architecture.⁠
⁠
For a new exhibition at @sessionsartsclub, the Hong Kong-born, London-based artist presents new works inspired by the visual language of the 1980s, drawing on interior design, cinematography, music videos, advertisements and fashion editorials. Executed in acrylic and ink on thick paper, the paintings are tender and charged with emotional possibility. ⁠
⁠
The paintings can be seen by anyone dining at Sessions Arts Club or by appointment now. Read an interview with the artist at the link in bio 📲⁠
⁠
📸 Artworks by @cary.kwok. Courtesy of @sessionsartsclub

NEW! #NOWNESSPresents: Artist-director Frederik Heyman merges his digitally constructed universes with the physical performance practice of Milou Van Duijnhoven for the experimental short film ‘The Scent Remains’ 
⁠

@bjork has opened a major new exhibition at Reykjavík’s National Gallery of Iceland, bringing together three large-scale audiovisual installations, including Ancestress and Sorrowful Soil, two deeply personal works dedicated to her late mother. Originally released during the Fossora era, both have been reimagined on a museum scale for the first time, alongside a newly commissioned film and sound installation offering an early glimpse into Björk’s next musical chapter. @newbottega has joined the project as patron and partner, continuing its recent collaboration with the artist following appearances at the Venice Biennale and beyond.

The exhibition runs through 20 September and is accompanied by *Metamorphlings*, a companion show from longtime collaborator James Merry. On 12 August, Björk will also host *Echolalia*, a one-day solar eclipse rave in Hafnarfjörður featuring performances from Arca, Sideproject and Ronja, alongside a DJ set from Björk herself.

Artificial intelligence is changing fashion image-making fast and not without controversy. As brands experiment with AI-generated campaigns, conversations around authorship, ethics, and the future of creative jobs continue to intensify. For the latest Industry Access conversation, legendary image-maker Nick Knight @nick_knight joins creative technologist Tom Wandrag @a_new_plane at SHOWstudio @showstudio in London to discuss the promises and limits of AI in fashion. With Knight’s groundbreaking work shooting stars like Björk, Kate Moss, Naomi Campbell, and Iman and A New Plane’s experiments with emerging technology, the pair explore whether AI can expand creativity without replacing the human instinct behind great images. Moderated by Models.com Editorial Director Irene Ojo-Felix, watch part 1 of conversation now at the link in bio and stay tuned next week for part 2.

Our second cover star on the spring issue of HIGHSNOBIETY, @taliaryder is the type of person that doesn’t just settle for being “Princess,” she wants to be “King.” 

At 23, Talia Ryder exists in a rare in-between. Recognizable, but not overexposed. In demand, but still choosing carefully. She moves between fashion, film, and dance without settling into any one identity, resisting the kind of shorthand that flattens artists into trends.

“I want to keep building, to keep working, to make things that actually last,” Ryder states. It’s clear that Ryder is one of those shapeshifting multihyphenates — dancer, actress, director, singer, model, occasional painter — who fuels the furnace of New York’s downtown arts scene.

Together with @someform.studio we had the pleasure of exhibiting Artificial Spaces at the latest edition of @noorriyadhfestival last November in Riyadh.
A new iteration of this contemplative installation where physical matter and digital light begin to interact as a single system.

At its center, a 25 kg polished marble sphere acts as a small planet that can be rotated and pushed to influence the creation. Its axis slowly shifts while the surrounding space reacts in real time, generating unique environments of light and movement.

Each space is generated live through CGI. Each one appears once, then disappears forever. Born from the beautiful randomness of a machine, fed with 3D models of architectural elements as columns, walls, furniture, objects, and programmed with care to allow the system to decide how the space is formed.

We would like to thank the organization of @noorriyadhfestival, @riyadhartofficial and @nouf.almoneef, as well as the curational team @sara.endipity @lzhenhua and @davide_quadrio @bruno.bolfo for this wonderful opportunity.

Dear friends, we are thrilled to unveil our latest exhibition—Latent City—at the BRUSK Museum in Bruges! ✨
Using a rich, ethically sourced archive of millions of publicly available images and cultural documents, we painted a living, dreaming portrait of this beautiful city.
Latent City is a real-time Living Data Sculpture. By analyzing the continuous, pulsing rhythms of Bruges—from weather fluctuations to transportation patterns—we use AI as a thinking brush, allowing the artwork to continuously dream and hallucinate as the city breathes around it.
Deepest gratitude to the wonderful city of Bruges, the incredible team at BRUSK, and our visionary curator,for your unwavering support in bringing this dream to reality. 🙏

Dear friends,
I’m deeply honored to announce that our artwork Unsupervised has been acquired by MoMA and is now in the museum’s permanent collection! The exhibition is closing on the 29th of October.

This acquisition marks a grand milestone in our studio’s journey and also for digital art. It inscribes a historic chapter as MoMA welcomes the first Generative AI and tokenized artwork into its esteemed permanent collection.

I am infinitely grateful to our curators Michelle Kuo, Paola Antonelli, and Stuart Comer for their wisdom and the entire MoMA team’s genuine support and collaboration since the beginning of the project.

We are also profoundly thankful to our collectors, Ryan Zurrer, Pablo Rodriguez-Fraile, and Desiree Casoni, and NVIDIA for supporting our journey.

For almost a year now, our artwork brought the museum audience joy, inspiration, and hope! Thank you, New York and all the visitors of MoMA from my heart! @themuseumofmodernart  #newyork

NYX

NYX partnered with TikTok influencers, who shared their makeup stories and discussed the significance of Pride. Dear friends, I’m very excited to share that our pioneering Infinito — AI Data Sculpture, our epic collaboration with Bvlgari allowed us to create the world’s first AI Data Sculpture of it’s own kind. Our AI model trained on 70-year-old Serpenti design archives and transformed the results into a 3-dimensional physical sculpture in 4m x 1.5m x 1.5m dimensions with robotic fabrication. Using light as a material, we augmented it into a living sculpture and let it dream impossible materials. We are grateful to Anne Hathaway for her support and collaboration! "The Size of Light" responds to a simple gesture. A movement of the hand becomes a shift in scale, in rhythm, in time. The sun grows and contracts with the opening and closing of the palm. Light shifts. The hour moves. The sky follows a gesture as simple as breathing.
I've been thinking about how we experience time not as a sequence of numbers but as light. The quality of morning. The weight of late afternoon. The particular silence of dusk. We feel time before we read it.
When the piece is installed, it changes with the real world. During the day, you hold the sun. At night, the moon. The same movement, the same palm — but the universe it touches has turned.
We are, after all, made of the same matter.

👇
Open in Barcelona, until August 27th, at @digitalimpact.art 💫

Real-time interactive creations, generated at the moment, unique and unrepeatable. 

The concept of beauty is variable, evolutionary and cultural. Who decides what is considered beautiful at each moment in history? Could the creative process be automated to change how we conceive beauty? By feeding creativity into the machine through architecture, photography, generative design, art and programming, the software can create unique and unrepeatable results, an infinite world of artificially generated architectural spaces created with a bit of our humanity, helping us to question what beauty really means to us.

My longest creative collaboration has been with our art director @mikemeire , alongside his deputy Tim Giesen. For almost 20 years - since Issue 13, Energy Experimentation - he has played a crucial role in shaping the identity of 032c. I still remember traveling to Cologne to present him  the very first issue, slightly in awe, because he was… Mike Meiré.

But change is necessary. As we reset 032c in multiple ways, we are also confronting new questions around the magazine’s design and aesthetics. At its core, the challenge is both simple and fundamental: what does it mean to publish a magazine in an AI world?

To explore this, we have decided to begin a new chapter with a different art director and team for the years ahead. This brings an extraordinary run with Mike and Tim (@newflower_edition) to a close - though, in true 032c Hotel California fashion (“You can’t check out”), we are already in conversation about a new project together.

We salute Mike and Tim for their remarkable contribution to 032c, with deep gratitude.

Joerg Koch, founder / EIC
